comments.author: @r8chlletters
comments.text: If you are getting into debt for basics all I can suggest is go all in, get personal loans to pay off your vehicle or any assets you want to keep and use those cards to pay your bills for a year and then go bankrupt. As long as you don’t make purchases that are recent and can be repossessed (groceries and bills and gas would not be able to be repossessed) you’ll be able to declare without having anything taken from you. This is one way to buy time. If you are employed it’s harder to declare. In 7 years you will have a clean slate, a decent credit score, and as long you don’t get any credit cards you’ll be debt free. Just be sure you have a car that is paid off a year ahead and a stable living situation where you can stay the next 7 years. No big purchases for a year beforehand and pay it all off with credit cards rolled into personal loans. Open a second bank account and right before you declare close the account all the cards and loans withdraw from. People want to be responsible but the system is absolutely rigged for debt and failure. This is why bankruptcy is sometimes (often) an answer. It will solve a lot for those who are mired in debt and cannot get out of it. I highly recommend looking into it. You never need to admit you did it even when asked as you are never legally obliged to tell anyone for any reason.
